### 🧭 The current solution for mcp gateway uses combination of web server and http client to create gateway between client and upstream mcp server. This proposal is about usage of Claudflare Pingora library https://github.com/cloudflare/pingora , which includes both web servers and http connectors to upstream server and offer pre-process and post-process filters - the same idea as current plugin system.

Pingora abstracts away transport semantics, letting us focus entirely on application semantics.


**Title:** Implement mcp gateway with Pingora library
**Goal:** Simplification of development process with well defined and documented approach.
**Why now:** The ongoing plan offers solution similar to python version (web server and http client library) this process assumes lower level abstraction than Pingora library. This means more work than usage of the library arleady working as a proxy. 
The current implementation of http client connections to upstream servers needs enhancement. The ticket was created in the past about excessive default ssl context creation. The recent changes with implemented session affinity also showed that maintenance of custom created http connections to upstream servers need attention.

See also: https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/4352 especially in comment: https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/4352#issuecomment-4295125274
```
Total Requests:            3,501
```
And these 3501 requests produced 8116 default ssl context creation:
```
cat log | grep PID | grep SSL  | wc -l
8116
```
The problem with upstream http connections may be addressed with Pingora library the connections to upstream servers is maintained by library. The bug found in the sample above is addressed by the library.

```
Pingora is the only open-source proxy framework where the upstream connection pool is not an afterthought — it’s the core of the architecture.

Everyone else treats upstream pooling as a library feature.
Pingora treats it as a first‑class subsystem.
```


---

### 🧑🏻‍💻 User Story 1

**As a:** Mcp client
**I want:** Work with mcp servers via gateway to icrease security
**So that:** Client connects to gateway based on Pingrora

#### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Streaming http variant
  Connection comes via pre and post filters without essenital changes in logic
  When request is coming incoming filter works
  Request is sent to upstream server and response via outcoming filter goes back to client

Scenario: Deprecated SSE MCP variant translated to Streaming HTTP variant
  Connection comes to one endpoint and in response another endpoint is sent back to client
  In Pingora inc post-process body is rewritten to redirect request to the same encpoint
  Client uses with Streaming HTTP even for deprecated SSE Mcp server.
```

Both scenarios were tested and prototyped in : https://github.com/sco3/pin-gateway
The sequence diagram on Readme.md shows another variant of implemenation of Deprecated SSE MCP protocol with memory session state - no body rewrite the redirection happens in pre-process filter. 
This approach has some benefits and drawbacks but was considered as less preferable and body rewrite approach is the current solution.l

### 📐 Design Sketch (optional)

Include a diagram, sketch, or flow (use [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) if desired):

```mermaid
graph TD
    %% Define Nodes
    Start((Client Request))
    
    subgraph Phase_1 [Phase 1: Setup]
        Init(fn new_ctx - Initialize Request Context)
    end

    subgraph Phase_2 [Phase_2: Pre-Processing REQUEST]
        EarlyFilter(fn early_request_filter - Rate Limiting)
        ReqFilter(fn request_filter - Modify Headers)
        Upstream(fn upstream_peer - Routing Decision)
    end

    subgraph Phase_3 [Phase 3: Upstream Connection]
        Connect(Connect to Origin)
        Origin[(Origin Server)]
        Receive(Receive Response)
    end

    subgraph Phase_4 [Phase 4: Post-Processing RESPONSE]
        ResFilter(fn response_filter - Modify Headers)
        BodyFilter(fn response_body_filter - Modify Body)
    end

    subgraph Phase_5 [Phase 5: Finalization]
        EndRes((Response to Client))
        Summary(fn request_summary - Logging/Metrics)
    end

    %% Flow logic
    Start --> Init
    Init --> EarlyFilter
    EarlyFilter --> ReqFilter
    ReqFilter --> Upstream
    
    Upstream --> Connect
    Connect <--> Origin
    Connect --> Receive
    
    Receive --> ResFilter
    ResFilter --> BodyFilter
    
    BodyFilter --> EndRes
    BodyFilter -.-> Summary
```
